Consult Summary:
- Young female with 2–3 days of constant lower abdominal aching with nausea, feeling hot/sweaty, and recent light pink coloration of urine/possible spotting; face-to-face assessment and investigations recommended to rule out pregnancy and other causes.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Dull, constant ache in lower abdomen (below the umbilicus) for the last few days.
  - Associated nausea without vomiting.
  - Feeling hot and sweaty; patient reported having "a bit of a temperature."
  - Noted slight pink discoloration in urine or possible vaginal spotting in the last couple of days.
  - Increased urinary frequency without dysuria, urgency, or malodorous urine.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptom onset: described as "the last couple of days" by patient; clinician also referenced three days — conflict noted (2 days vs 3 days).
  - Constipation reported about one week ago but resolved; normal bowel motions over the last few days; last bowel movement yesterday.
  - Pink urine/spotting noted over the last couple of days; patient expected her period soon (last menstrual period approximately 3+ weeks ago).
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No clear exacerbating or relieving factors documented.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - No vomiting.
  - No dysuria, no stinging on urination, no urgency, no foul smell to urine.
  - No vaginal discharge.
  - No light-headedness or syncope.
- Menstrual/sexual/reproductive history:
  - Last menstrual period about three and a bit weeks ago.
  - Sexually active with one partner.
  - Contraception: implant (patient stated "Implanon").
  - Patient uncertain about pregnancy but believes pregnancy unlikely; clinician stated pregnancy should be ruled out.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No vomiting, no urinary pain, no urgency, no vaginal discharge.
  - No other chronic medical problems reported.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported by patient.
- Family history: brother with type 1 diabetes.

Medications:
- Implanon (contraceptive implant) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Patient states she takes no other regular medications.

Allergies:
- Amoxicillin.

Social History:
- Lives with boyfriend.
- Sexually active with one regular partner.
- Non-smoker.
- Patient reports high fluid intake (drinks lots of water).
- No other social, alcohol, recreational drug, occupational, or financial factors documented.

Family History:
- Brother: type 1 diabetes.
- No other family medical history reported to clinician.

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination findings documented.
- Vitals: not recorded in the transcript (patient reported feeling "a bit of a temperature" but no measured temperature documented).

Investigations:
- No investigations performed or results available in the transcript.
- Clinician recommended further tests but specifics not documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute lower abdominal pain with nausea and systemic symptoms (hot/sweaty)
  - Assessment: Dull, constant lower abdominal ache for several days with nausea and subjective fever; etiology unclear.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange face-to-face assessment with GP today for abdominal and pelvic examination.
    - Perform appropriate investigations as indicated at face-to-face visit (clinician did not specify which tests).
    - Advise patient to seek urgent care if symptoms worsen.
- Issue 2: Possible pregnancy / vaginal bleeding or pink urine
  - Assessment: Patient reports slight pink discoloration in urine or spotting and is due for period soon; uses Implanon; clinician emphasized need to rule out pregnancy.
  - Plan:
    - Perform pregnancy test at face-to-face visit.
    - Further gynecologic evaluation as indicated (pelvic exam, speculum exam, or urine analysis) to clarify source of pink discoloration.
- Issue 3: Recent constipation (resolved) and increased urinary frequency
  - Assessment: Constipation occurred ~1 week ago and has since resolved; currently increased urinary frequency without dysuria.
  - Plan:
    - Evaluate bladder/urinary symptoms at face-to-face visit; consider urine dipstick/urinalysis if indicated.
    - No immediate pharmacologic treatment documented.
- General plan items:
  - Face-to-face GP appointment arranged/encouraged for same day (patient agreeable).
  - Safety-netting: return or seek urgent care if light-headedness, fainting, worsening symptoms, or any other concerning developments.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No documented vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate).
  - No physical examination findings (abdominal or pelvic exam).
  - No pregnancy test result.
  - No laboratory or imaging results (urinalysis, urine culture, pregnancy test, blood tests, ultrasound).
  - No definitive diagnosis or differential list beyond clinician stating "could be a few different things."
  - No medication recommendations or prescriptions documented.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Symptom duration: patient states "last couple of days" (2 days) while clinician at one point summarized "for three days" — conflict noted.
  - Pink urine vs expected menstrual bleeding: patient described pink in her urine and also being due on her period; source of pink discoloration unclear — conflict/uncertainty noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall audible and intelligible; occasional overlapping speech and filler words but sufficient for clinical documentation.
